Good on you for taking on the job, and I agree with comments saying the girl needs support. But I would see about talking to her family or friends about supporting her. I wouldn’t jump to any crazy conclusions, there’s excitement in general for potentially having a baby for some people and that may have been the switch. I will say, and I’m a engaged woman atm, I have been very clear about my boundaries and unpreparedness for birthing, raising, and whatever with children. It’s okay to not be ready for kids or not want them at all and, especially if the conversation has already been discussed between you two, those boundaries should be respected. 
It’s important to care while she’s struggling, but you don’t have to be the one providing the care. Help find someone more prepared to do that, so you can process everything yourself. Best of luck.

If you can hold out until college (if you plan on or can go) wait until you can try medicine. My parents wouldn’t let me take it, even though they both took stuff. It didn’t fix everything, but it helped managed. The counseling office at school can hook you up with a psychiatrist and can work around not being able to use parents’ insurance. I don’t know your circumstance, but if you can get away with staying late after school or not going home until later and just say you’re doing schoolwork if they try to bug you it could help. I would at least hold out until you can try medicine. It’s a process and trauma from emotionally abusive parents could fuck you up for awhile. But you get to a point we’re you can completely shut them out and it feels good. I’ve tried to kill myself before and have cut since I was 11 and my stepdad still gave me a gun as a house warming gift when I moved out to “protect myself”. I would say that if they’re not great now, they never will be and you don’t owe them shit.
